notes.1-8: The extracts were short, straightforward interactions. Overall, candidates performed well in this exercise. Most candidates answered Question 1 successfully. In Question 2 , many candidates were familiar with un œuf ; those who answered incorrectly mostly chose option B . For Question 3 , under two thirds of the candidates correctly identified the directions; option D was the most frequent incorrect answer . In Question 4 , some candidates did not understand fenêtre ; B was the most frequent error. Question 5 was attempted well. In Question 6 , many candidates were familiar with confiture; option D was the most common incorrect answer. Most candidates understood the time in Question 7 and all answered Question 8 correctly .
notes.9-14: In this exercise, candidates heard a longer extract which featured information about a school exchange. Candidates performed very well in this exercise. In Question 9 , most candidates understood en train and many candidates identified la cantine in Question 10 . Most candidates answered Question 11 correctly. Question 12 was attempted well; candidates who did not understand poisson often chose option C instead. Volley was well understood in Question 13 , and all candidates answered Question 14 correctly.
notes.15-19: This was a matching exercise in which candidates heard a conversation between Farida and her brother discussing clothes for a wedding. The exercise represented a step up in the incline of difficulty of the test. In Question 15 , just over half the candidates correctly matched ça ne me va pas du tout […] quelle horreur with statement C . Statement F was the most frequent incorrect answer, perhaps because of quand j’étais petite which referred to Farida, not a garment. Over half the cohort understood j’ai besoin d’une plus grande taille in Question 16 and selected the correct answer F . Similar numbers answered Question 17 correctly; the most common error was E . In Question 18 , half the candidates successfully matched c’est un style trop vieux pour moi with E ; a third of the candidates incorrectly chose C . Two thirds of the candidates answered Question 19 correctly; statement A was the most frequent error, perhaps because of the reference to dancing ( je serai à l’aise pour danser).
notes.20-28: In this exercise, candidates heard an interview in two parts with Arturo, a young man from Madagascar who talked about the skate park in his village. The exercise represented another step up in the incline of difficulty of the test. Overall, candidates performed well in this exercise. For Question 20 , many candidates understood région rurale and correctly chose option C ; distractor A was the most frequent error. Question 21 was attempted well, and most candidates answered Question 22 correctly. For Question 23 , three quarters of the candidates correctly selected option A . The most common error was distractor B . Question 24 was the most challenging: over a third of the candidates understood même les chaussures and correctly chose B ; half heard le terrain and incorrectly chose distractor A . For Question 25 , over three quarters of the candidates chose the correct option C ; distractor A was the most common error. Three quarters of the candidates also answered Question 26 successfully. Those who answered incorrectly usually missed the negative (font du skate pour avoir l’air cool, mais pas moi) and chose distractor C . Question 27 was attempted well. Many candidates understood the incentive to work well at school for the children in the village and chose option C ; all the others chose distractor A . Many candidates answered Question 28 successfully; most of those who answered incorrectly heard un coach and chose distractor A .
notes.29-34: In this extract, candidates heard an interview with Théa, an architect in Luxembourg. This was an appropriately demanding exercise at this stage of the paper and, overall, candidates coped well with the demands of this exercise. For Question 29 , many candidates chose the correct option D . Those who answered incorrectly heard dans mon travail and chose distractor A . For Question 30 , three quarters of the candidates correctly chose option C ; distractor D was the most common error. Question 31 was the most challenging in this exercise; over half of the cohort correctly chose option A . A quarter incorrectly chose distractor C , an area of work which Théa dismissed with sauf peut-être les zones industrielles. In Question 32 , over two thirds of the candidates correctly selected option C . Those who answered incorrectly chose distractors B or D in equal numbers: candidates needed to listen carefully as the adjectives in personnalités opposées and spécialisations différentes contradicted the statements. In Question 33 , two thirds of the candidates successfully chose B . Those who answered incorrectly often missed the time phrase and past tense ( l’année dernière, la ville a fait de nouvelles pistes cyclables) and chose distractor A . Question 34 was attempted well and nearly three quarters of the candidates chose the correct option D . Distractor A was the most frequent error.
notes.35-37: Candidates heard an interview with André who had done a house exchange with a family in La Réunion. For each question, candidates had to identify two correct statements from a choice of five. This was an appropriately demanding and challenging exercise at this stage of the paper. In Question 35 , half the candidates correctly chose option A and just under half option B . Statements D and E proved strong distractors. In Question 36 , just under half of the cohort successfully selected option A ; not quite as many correctly chose C . Candidates needed to listen carefully to understand which items each family had made available. Many candidates missed the negative in même si on n’était pas près de la mer and chose distractor D . Question 37 was attempted well; two thirds of the candidates correctly chose option C and just under half option E . Statement B proved a strong distractor for many candidates: they needed to listen to the whole sentence as the time phrase une ou deux fois nous avons loué une voiture contradicted pendant toutes les vacances.
